# New CEO Michael J. Whitehead Outlines Refocus on Core Businesses as Matthews International Reports Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year Ended September 30, 2026


[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_889e1340ce359ba070eb3fd016ad98fc/matw/news/2026-11-19_New_CEO_Michael_J_Whitehead_Outlines_Refocus_on_320.pdf) November 19, 2026 4:15pm EST


### Related Documents


[Audio](https://viavid.webcasts.com/starthere.jsp?ei=1780058&tp_key=483ccadb0e)


[Earnings Webcast](https://viavid.webcasts.com/starthere.jsp?ei=1780058&tp_key=483ccadb0e)


[Call Presentation](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_889e1340ce359ba070eb3fd016ad98fc/matw/db/739/7285/presentation/Q4-26_Slides_MATW_Earnings_Telecast.pdf)[PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_889e1340ce359ba070eb3fd016ad98fc/matw/db/739/7285/presentation/Q4-26_Slides_MATW_Earnings_Telecast.pdf)


**Financial Highlights:**


- ***CEO Michael J. Whitehead: "We are refocusing on core businesses by strengthening them, simplifying operations, and driving sustainable growth"***
- ***CEO continues to evaluate strategic alternatives across the remaining portfolio and actions for fiscal 2027; no full-year guidance at this time***
- ***4th quarter consolidated sales of $256.7 million; $1.05 billion for fiscal 2026***
- ***Memorialization reports higher 4th quarter sales and adjusted EBITDA***
- ***The Company generated positive consolidated operating cash flows in the 4th quarter***
- ***Year-to-year debt reduction of $100 million; interest expense reduction of $17.1 million***
- ***Webcast: Friday, November 20, 2026, 9:00 a.m., (203) 518-9757***


PITTSBURGH--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Matthews International Corporation (NASDAQ GSM: MATW) today announced financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended September 30, 2026, and shared the perspectives of new President and Chief Executive Officer Michael J. Whitehead on the Company’s results and direction.


**Perspectives from CEO Michael J. Whitehead**


In discussing the Company’s results and his priorities, Michael J. Whitehead, President and Chief Executive Officer, stated:


“Since joining Matthews a few months ago, I've had the opportunity to visit our facilities and experience first-hand the outstanding work across our businesses. Following the reshaping of our portfolio over the last two years, we are now refocusing on our core businesses — strengthening them, simplifying operations, and driving sustainable growth. We continue to evaluate strategic alternatives across the remaining portfolio and actions for fiscal 2027.


"We finished 2026 strongly, with 4th quarter consolidated results at the high end of our expectations. Sales for the Memorialization segment outperformed the same quarter a year ago, corporate and other non-operating costs declined, and product identification sales grew 14%. Our engineering business continues to face customer delays related to ongoing litigation.


"For fiscal 2026, sales from retained businesses exceeded $1 billion. Memorialization achieved record annual sales, up 4%, driven in part by The Dodge Company acquisition, while adjusted EBITDA also reached a record level with margin expansion. Propelis continues to progress with integration, and we are working with our partners on exit strategies.


"The December 2025 sale of our warehouse automation business helped reduce debt by $100.4 million year over year. We remain focused on further debt reduction while delivering competitive shareholder returns through quarterly dividends.


"As we enter fiscal 2027, economic uncertainty and litigation affecting our engineering business remain significant considerations. The leadership transition is progressing well, but work remains to define our go-forward strategies. Accordingly, we are not providing full-year fiscal 2027 guidance at this time."


**Divestiture of the SGK Business**


The fiscal 2025 consolidated financial information presented in this release reflects the financial results of the SGK business through the closing date. As a result of the integration process of Propelis and transition to its stand-alone reporting systems, our 40% portion of the financial results of Propelis is reported on a one-quarter lag. Consequently, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company's portion of earnings (losses) for its equity-method investment in Propelis includes the months from April 2026 through June 2026. For the twelve months ended September 30, 2026, the Company's portion of earnings (losses) for its equity-method investment in Propelis includes the months from July 2025 through June 2026.


The Company’s consolidated adjusted EBITDA for the fiscal fourth quarter of 2026 includes approximately a $12.7 million adjusted EBITDA contribution from Propelis. Based on preliminary estimates of adjusted EBITDA provided by Propelis for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, our 40% portion of their adjusted EBITDA would be $11.6 million. The Company’s consolidated adjusted EBITDA for the fiscal twelve months ended June 30, 2026 includes a $45.1 million adjusted EBITDA contribution from Propelis. Based on preliminary financial estimates of adjusted EBITDA provided by Propelis for the period October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026, our 40% portion of their adjusted EBITDA would be $43.7 million. Please note that these projections are unaudited and subject to review and, as a result, may change.


**Webcast**


The Company will host a conference call and webcast on Friday, November 20, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Eastern Time to review its financial and operating results and discuss its corporate strategies and outlook. A question-and-answer session will follow. The conference call can be accessed by dialing (203) 518-9757, Conference ID: Matthews. The audio webcast can be monitored at[www.matw.com](http://www.matw.com/)


. As soon as available after the call, a transcript of the call will be posted on the Investor Relations section of the Company’s website at[www.matw.com](http://www.matw.com/)

**About Matthews International Corporation**


Matthews International Corporation operates through two core global businesses – Memorialization and Industrial Technologies. Both are focused on driving operational efficiency and long-term growth through continuous innovation and strategic expansion. The Memorialization segment is a leading provider of memorialization products, including memorials, caskets and cremation and incineration equipment, principally to cemetery and funeral home customers that help families move from grief to remembrance. The Industrial Technologies segment evolved from our original marking business, which today is a leading global innovator committed to empowering visionaries to transform industries through the application of precision technologies and intelligent processes. In addition, the Company also has a significant investment in Propelis, a brand solutions business formed through the merger of SGK and SGS & Co. Propelis delivers integrated solutions including brand creative, packaging, print solutions, branded environments, and content production. Matthews International has over 4,200 employees in 15 countries on four continents that are committed to delivering the highest quality products and services.

**Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


Included in this report are measures of financial performance that are not defined by GAAP, including, without limitation, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income and EPS, constant currency sales, constant currency adjusted EBITDA, net debt and net debt leverage ratio. The Company defines net debt leverage ratio as outstanding debt (net of cash) relative to adjusted EBITDA. The Company uses non-GAAP financial measures to assist in comparing its performance on a consistent basis for purposes of business decision-making by removing the impact of certain items that management believes do not directly reflect the Company’s core operations including acquisition and divestiture costs, ERP system integration costs, strategic initiative and other charges (which includes non-recurring charges related to certain commercial and operational initiatives and exit activities), stock-based compensation and the non-service portion of pension and postretirement expense. Constant currency sales and constant currency adjusted EBITDA remove the impact of changes due to foreign exchange translation rates. To calculate sales and adjusted EBITDA on a constant currency basis, amounts for periods in the current fiscal year are translated into U.S. dollars using exchange rates applicable to the comparable periods of the prior fiscal year. Management believes that presenting non-GAAP financial measures is useful to investors because it (i) provides investors with meaningful supplemental information regarding financial performance by excluding certain items that management believes do not directly reflect the Company's core operations, (ii) permits investors to view performance using the same tools that management uses to budget, forecast, make operating and strategic decisions, and evaluate historical performance, and (iii) otherwise provides supplemental information that may be useful to investors in evaluating the Company’s results. The Company's calculations of its non-GAAP financial measures, however, may not be comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies. The Company believes that the presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures, when considered together with the corresponding GAAP financial measures and the reconciliations to those measures, provided herein, provide investors with an additional understanding of the factors and trends affecting the Company’s business that could not be obtained absent these disclosures.
